note: A draft that trips a `block` rule cannot reach an analyst's approval queue at all — it is returned to rework. This is the mechanism that answers the compliance officer's objection: the question is not whether the model is well-behaved, it is whether a badly-behaved draft can physically reach a customer.

block.why: Admission of liability in writing, pre-investigation.

block.pattern: \b(?:we guarantee|guaranteed|we promise|rest assured that we will|you will definitely)\b

block.why: States a remediation outcome before an investigation has concluded.

block.pattern: \b(?:you (?:should|may want to) (?:consult|contact) (?:a|an|your) (?:lawyer|attorney)|you have no (?:legal )?(?:claim|right)|this is not covered by law)\b
block.why: Legal advice or a legal conclusion.
Commits to a timeframe the bank has not agreed to.
Bare long digit string in customer-facing text — possible un-redacted identifier.
Blames the customer. UDAAP-adjacent tone risk.
Unfilled template slot reached the draft.

warn.why: Tone: reads as deflection to a frustrated customer.
Internal or regulatory jargon in customer-facing text.
Draft is long; analysts will not read it, they will rewrite it.
A redaction placeholder is inside the draft. It will be rehydrated with the real value at send time, which is correct for a letter to the account holder — but confirm it reads naturally.
